correctness.rationale: The Fourier series uses length measure and integrates to one. The exponential mixture of strictly positive periodized stable transition densities gives a positive minimum: the mixture restricted to t in [1,2] already has a uniform positive lower bound. Write a_k=σ^(−α)k^(−α)+r_k with ∑k|r_k|<∞; the remainder is C¹, even, and has derivative zero at the cusp. The leading decrement is a Riemann sum for ∫₀∞(1−cos t)t^(−α)dt=π/[2Γ(α) sin(π(α−1)/2)], obtained by the Laplace representation of t^(−α) and the beta integral. Dirichlet summation bounds the scaled sine-series tail beyond k=T/|x| by O(T^(−β)), where β=α−1; rescaling the finite part gives the derivative constant −βB on the positive side, with the opposite sign on the negative side. At α=2 the sawtooth sine series gives the same one-sided result. Passing to g=√f divides the cusp constant by 2√f(0). For β<1/2, after x=hu the squared increment is dominated on the rescaled tails by C|u|^(2β−2), with bounded integrand on compact sets; away from the cusp the original integral is O(h²). This gives the exact Jβ and the power 2β+1. At β=1/2, on M|h|<|x|<δ the derivative asymptote and |h/x|≤1/M give relative errors made arbitrarily small by taking δ small and M large after the h limit. The two sides each give A²/4 times h² log(1/|h|); the remaining pieces are O_{M,δ}(h²). Independently, Parseval gives ||f(·−h)−f||²=(2/π)∑a_k²(1−cos kh); at α=3/2 the harmonic sum gives σ^(−3)h² log(1/|h|)/π. The square-root difference divides this leading term by 4f(0) since it is concentrated near the cusp, agreeing with A²/2. For β>1/2 the integrable derivative near the cusp is also square integrable, so g is in periodic H¹ and the translation derivative is −g′ in L², giving I/4. At and below β=1/2 the squared Hellinger discrepancy divided by h² diverges, ruling out DQM. The integrand of truncated information is 4g′²∼4A²β²|x|^(2β−2), which gives both asserted constants by two-sided integration. This is fixed-scale, fixed-shape circular location inference for 1<α≤2 using non-halved Hellinger loss, not uniform asymptotics or a statement about joint estimators. The source checker was inspected, not executed.

evidence: The 87e6f4c012d9 generic passage proves the non-halved critical law (b²/2)h² log(1/|h|) for a square-root cusp with a locally Lipschitz remainder and a square-integrable derivative off the cusp. At α=3/2, the local expansion of the principal cosine polylogarithm has an analytic remainder and the Fourier coefficient residual is C¹. Expanding √f therefore gives −A√|x| plus a Lipschitz remainder. Localize the circle to the cusp; the complementary shift costs O(h²). The prior critical law thus covers this step with b=−A.

The 92a2596e06eb threshold is for an endpoint power-log family in its log parameter, not α in wrapped Linnik. Lim–Teo covers the cusp amplitude before applying the wrapped square-root normalization but not the circular location problem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The critical asymptotic mechanism is a true prior implication, not just an analogous problem. The proof still needs to obtain the wrapped calibration, its subcritical exact modulus and truncated circular information, and assemble the three regimes. None of the inspected stronger statements already supplies that combined model-specific result. The inaccessible follow-up cannot be treated as negative evidence.

evidence: SenGupta–Roy (2023), §3 Theorem 2 and eq. (5), gives the identical Fourier density in θ−μ, with scale σ in (σp)^α.

The Lim–Teo real-line near-origin expansion at n=ν=1 recovers the same leading cusp exponent and B after matching scale. For the wrapped law the square-root amplitude divides by 2√f(0), where f(0) is the sum over all periodic images, rather than the real-line peak.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The wrapped model is exactly prior, and its cusp is related to the known unwrapped cusp, not a new singularity. Real-line Hellinger shifts cannot simply be restated as circular ones: wrapping changes the denominator of the leading square-root amplitude, and the regular Fisher integral is over the circular density.

originality.rationale: Narrow pass for the complete normalized wrapped-Linnik location classification and its model-specific constants. The model, real-line cusp ingredient, generic square-root-cusp logarithm, and regular Sobolev/DQM principle are not original. A prior generic critical formula really does apply after checking the wrapped square-root remainder and matching the Hellinger convention. The inspected cases and general frameworks do not supply the full calibrated circular result with both divergent-information constants. This is a bounded assessment with a relevant inaccessible follow-up, not a claim that the underlying cusp mechanism or the number 3/2 by itself is novel.
residual_risks: No conclusion about the full contents of the same-family follow-up PMC11389635; full text was not successfully retrieved. The cited Bell–Nadarajah and Shemyakin full texts were also not available in this comparison.
Equivalent circular kernel asymptotics could be indexed under fractional Bessel potentials, resolvent kernels, or general periodic nonregular location models.

value.rationale: For a standard circular family this answers whether location inference falls under the usual finite-information translation model, and quantifies the loss of regularity in the actual wrapped normalization. In particular it separates the pure fractional modulus from the critical logarithm and identifies how the scale and the entire wrapped density peak enter the leading constants. Checking and calibrating those regimes for this model is useful beyond repeating a generic Sobolev criterion; it does not establish an optimal estimator or a joint-parameter inference theory.
